![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14261267/assets/fe8506a91207de3a2151192be03a535a48912f7920a084c2a56d7bc16100dcb6.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curve $y=5{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2}$ and the $x$-axis, shown above. What integral gives the volume of the solid generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?
question.worked_solution:
First, we determine the points where the curve intersects the $x$-axis by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}(x+1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=-1$, $x=0.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=-1$ to $x=0.$ 

Using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}x(5{x}^{3}+5{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =10\pi {\int }_{-1}^{0}({x}^{4}+{x}^{3})\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$
